# 3-Week Reconditioning Block

**Before starting:** Persistent fatigue after a flu-like illness, in a 41-year-old, warrants a medical check before loading. Ask for a GP sign-off, and if he has any chest pain, palpitations, breathlessness, or unusual exercise intolerance, he needs an ECG and possibly cardiac workup before training resumes. Viral illness can occasionally affect the heart, so this matters even if he feels mostly recovered.

**Working loads** are based on pre-illness maxes (bench 100, squat 140, deadlift 170 kg). Round to the nearest 2.5 kg.

| Lift | Week 1 (~60%) | Week 2 (~70%) | Week 3 (~80%) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Bench | 60 kg | 70 kg | 80 kg |
| Squat | 85 kg | 97.5 kg | 112 kg |
| Deadlift | 100 kg | 120 kg | 135 kg |

Training is 3 days per week, with at least one rest day between sessions. Rest 2–3 minutes between main lifts.

---

## Week 1: Re-entry (volume ~60%, RPE 5–6)

The goal is movement quality and tolerance, with no grinding reps and no near-failure sets. Stop every set with at least 4 reps in reserve.

**Day A (Squat focus)**
- Back squat: 3 × 5 @ 85 kg
- Romanian deadlift: 3 × 8 @ light-moderate load
- Leg press: 2 × 10
- Lat pulldown: 3 × 10
- Dead bug: 2 × 8 per side

**Day B (Bench focus)**
- Bench press: 3 × 5 @ 60 kg
- Seated dumbbell overhead press: 3 × 8
- Chest-supported row: 3 × 10
- Face pulls: 2 × 15
- Plank: 2 × 30 s

**Day C (Hinge focus)**
- Deadlift: 3 × 3 @ 100 kg
- Front squat or goblet squat: 2 × 8
- Walking lunges: 2 × 8 per leg
- Single-arm dumbbell row: 3 × 10 per side
- Farmer's carry: 3 × 30 m

---

## Week 2: Rebuilding (volume ~80%, RPE 6–7)

Sets return to 3–4 per main lift, with the top sets around RPE 7. Accessories stay moderate.

**Day A (Squat focus)**
- Back squat: 4 × 5 @ 97.5 kg
- Romanian deadlift: 3 × 8 @ moderate load
- Bulgarian split squat: 2 × 8 per leg
- Pull-ups or assisted pull-ups: 3 × 6–8
- Pallof press: 2 × 10 per side

**Day B (Bench focus)**
- Bench press: 4 × 5 @ 70 kg
- Dumbbell overhead press: 3 × 8
- Cable row: 3 × 10
- Triceps pushdown: 2 × 12
- Face pulls: 2 × 15

**Day C (Hinge focus)**
- Deadlift: 3 × 3 @ 120 kg
- Paused squat or box squat: 3 × 5 @ 70% of squat max (~98 kg)
- Hip thrust: 3 × 8
- Chin-ups: 3 × 6–8
- Suitcase carry: 3 × 30 m per side

---

## Week 3: Return to Baseline (volume ~90%, top sets RPE 7–8)

The aim is to get back to working loads near pre-illness levels without testing maxes. Hold back if the bar speed drops noticeably.

**Day A (Squat focus)**
- Back squat: 4 × 4 @ 112 kg (last set RPE 8)
- Romanian deadlift: 3 × 8
- Leg press: 3 × 10
- Lat pulldown: 3 × 8
- Ab wheel or dead bug: 2 × 8

**Day B (Bench focus)**
- Bench press: 4 × 4 @ 80 kg (last set RPE 8)
- Incline dumbbell press: 3 × 8
- Chest-supported row: 3 × 8
- Lateral raises: 3 × 12
- Face pulls: 2 × 15

**Day C (Hinge focus)**
- Deadlift: 3 × 3 @ 135 kg (last set RPE 7–8)
- Front squat: 3 × 5
- Walking lunges: 2 × 8 per leg
- Single-arm row: 3 × 8 per side
- Farmer's carry: 3 × 40 m

End of Week 3: Schedule a retest in Week 4 or 5 if he feels fully recovered. Use a rep-max test or a submaximal estimate rather than a true 1RM.

---

## Nutrition

- **Calories:** He lost 4 kg, so aim for a modest surplus of 200–300 kcal/day above maintenance for the block. Weigh him weekly and adjust if he is not regaining weight.
- **Protein:** 1.8–2.2 g/kg bodyweight daily, spread over 3–4 meals.
- **Hydration:** Pay attention to fluid intake, especially if appetite is still reduced.

## Recovery

- **Sleep:** 7.5–9 hours. This is the single most important recovery factor after illness.
- **Daily check:** Resting heart rate and a simple readiness rating (1–10) on waking. If resting HR is more than about 10% above his baseline, or readiness is 4 or lower, drop that session to light mobility or walking.
- **Stop criteria:** Fever, chest pain, palpitations, dizziness, or fatigue that worsens across sessions. Any of these means stopping training and seeing a doctor.
- **Deload:** No separate deload is needed in this block because it is already a reduced-volume progression. Keep the Week 3 loads as the entry point for normal training afterwards.

**Week 1 working sets (3 sessions/week, one main lift per session)**

| Lift | Session | Sets × Reps | Load | % of pre-illness max | Target effort |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Bench press | Day B | 3 × 5 | **60 kg** | 60% of 100 kg | Stop with 4+ reps in reserve |
| Back squat | Day A | 3 × 5 | **85 kg** | ~61% of 140 kg | Stop with 4+ reps in reserve |
| Deadlift | Day C | 3 × 3 | **100 kg** | ~59% of 170 kg | Stop with 4+ reps in reserve |

**Warm-up before each main lift** (not counted as working sets):
- Bench: 1 × 10 empty bar, then 1 × 5 at ~30 kg
- Squat: 1 × 8 at ~40 kg, 1 × 5 at ~60 kg, 1 × 3 at ~72 kg
- Deadlift: 1 × 8 at ~50 kg, 1 × 5 at ~70 kg, 1 × 3 at ~85 kg

**Adjustments:** If bar speed is slow in the first working set or he reports lingering fatigue, reduce the load by 5–10% for that session and keep the rep scheme. If the first working set feels easy, do not add load this week. Week 1 is about tolerance, so the numbers above are the ceiling.

Here's how to bring his running back into the programme without overloading him during reconditioning. Pre-illness he ran 10 km weekly, so the plan builds back to that over the three weeks, with the running kept easy and separate from the lifting.

**Principles**
- Run on non-lifting days or after lifting with at least 6 hours between sessions. Lifting sessions should not be combined with a hard run.
- Keep runs at conversational pace (Zone 2, roughly RPE 3–4 out of 10). Post-viral fatigue responds badly to intensity.
- Build total weekly distance gradually. Don't jump straight to 10 km.
- Ask him to report any breathlessness out of proportion to pace, chest discomfort, palpitations, or dizziness during or after runs. These mean stopping and seeing a doctor, same as the lifting stop criteria.

**Weekly running volume**

| Week | Sessions | Weekly distance | Structure |
|---|---|---|---|
| Week 1 | 2 | 4 km total | 2 × 2 km easy, or 1 × 3 km + 1 × 1 km walk-run. Keep the effort very conversational. |
| Week 2 | 2 | 6–7 km total | 2 × 3–3.5 km easy. Optional 3rd short easy run of 2 km if he feels well. |
| Week 3 | 3 | 8–9 km total | 2 × 3 km easy + 1 × 2–3 km easy. Can include 4 × 30 s relaxed strides at the end of one run. |

**Scheduling around the lifts**

Lifting is Mon/Wed/Fri in a typical split, so running fits well on Tuesday, Thursday, and Saturday. Two runs a week fits Tuesday and Saturday. In Week 3, add Sunday or Thursday if recovery is good.

Example Week 3:
- Mon: Day A (squat)
- Tue: 3 km easy run
- Wed: Day B (bench)
- Thu: 2–3 km easy run or rest
- Fri: Day C (deadlift)
- Sat: 3 km easy run
- Sun: Rest or walk

**Progression back to 10 km**

Once Week 3 is complete and he feels recovered, reach 10 km total per week over Weeks 4–5, adding about 1–1.5 km per week. Keep one run easy and one as a longer steady run. Introduce tempo or interval work only after he is back to his full 10 km without fatigue carrying into the next session.

**Readiness rule**

Apply the same daily check as the lifting: if resting HR is more than about 10% above baseline or readiness is 4 or lower, replace the run with walking or skip it.

Here's a target intake for the reconditioning block. Without his current bodyweight, height, or activity levels, these are estimates, so confirm them with a current weigh-in and adjust from there.

**Starting assumptions**
- He lost 4 kg. If he was roughly 85 kg pre-illness, he is now about 81 kg. Replace this with his actual weight.
- Maintenance for a 41-year-old active male (lifting 3 days, running ~6–10 km/week) is typically around 2,800–3,100 kcal/day at ~81–85 kg. Confirm with a TDEE calculation or by tracking weight trends over 2 weeks.

**Calories**
- **Target:** maintenance + 200–300 kcal, roughly 3,000–3,400 kcal/day.
- Start at the lower end in Week 1, when appetite may still be reduced after illness, and move toward the upper end by Week 3 if he is not regaining weight.
- Aim for a weight gain of about 0.25–0.5 kg per week. Faster regain is mostly fat and fluid, and the body is still recovering.
- If he feels full or nauseated easily, split intake into 5–6 smaller meals rather than forcing larger portions.

**Protein**
- 1.8–2.2 g/kg/day. At 81 kg, that is roughly 150–175 g/day.
- Spread across 4 meals of 35–45 g each, with one serving before bed if convenient (e.g., Greek yoghurt, cottage cheese, or casein).
- Lean sources: chicken, fish, eggs, lean beef, dairy, legumes, tofu.

**Carbohydrates**
- Around 4–6 g/kg/day, so roughly 330–490 g/day at 81 kg. Scale to his running volume: the higher end on days he runs, the lower end on rest days.
- Prioritise carbs around training and running sessions to fuel work and support glycogen recovery.

**Fats**
- About 0.8–1.2 g/kg/day, roughly 65–100 g/day, to make up the remaining calories. Don't drop below about 0.7 g/kg, as very low fat intake can affect hormone production and recovery.

**Hydration and micronutrients**
- Roughly 2.5–3 L/day, more on run days and in hot conditions.
- Post-viral appetite loss can lead to low intake of iron, B vitamins, and magnesium. A food-first diet with a varied range of vegetables, whole grains, and dairy or fortified alternatives usually covers this. A GP can check ferritin and B12 if fatigue persists beyond a few weeks.

**Monitoring**
- Weigh 2–3 times per week under similar conditions and use the weekly average.
- If weight is flat for 2 weeks, add about 150 kcal/day. If he gains faster than 0.5 kg/week, reduce by about 100–150 kcal/day.
- Track energy, sleep, and session performance alongside weight. Falling performance with weight gain can signal under-recovery, not a need for more food.

It isn't reasonable to skip Week 1 on the strength of how he feels today, and I'd hold the line on the reconditioning progression. There are several reasons.

**Subjective recovery is unreliable after viral illness.** Feeling normal on one morning doesn't tell you his tolerance for load. Post-viral fatigue often shows up as a relapse after a session that looked fine on paper, sometimes 24 to 72 hours later. Reporting "normal energy" is a useful signal, but it isn't a substitute for a graded return.

**Pre-illness loads are a poor starting point after 3 weeks off.** Three weeks of detraining, plus 4 kg of weight loss, means he has lost some strength and likely some muscle, and his joints and connective tissue have had a layoff too. Bench 100, squat 140, and deadlift 170 are maxes he built at full health and full bodyweight. Jumping straight to them is a classic setup for a strain or a bad session.

**Heart and cardiovascular risk still matter.** The bigger concern is not muscle soreness. Viral illness can involve the heart (myocarditis, pericarditis), and those can present with minimal symptoms and are most dangerous under heavy exertion. He hasn't been medically cleared yet, as far as I know. Heavy lifting, especially near maximal effort, should wait until that's sorted.

**Feeling fine today is consistent with the plan.** The programme is designed so that if he feels good, the progression is faster. Week 1 is 60% loads at RPE 5–6, which will be easy for him if he's genuinely recovered. He'll likely finish Week 1 feeling he could have done more, and that's the point. The data from Week 1 then tells you whether Week 2 and 3 loads are appropriate.

**What I'd suggest instead:**
- Check whether he has had a GP review and cardiac screening if indicated. This is the non-negotiable step.
- If he's cleared, run Week 1 as written, but let the first working set of each lift set the pace. If he's moving fast and the bar feels light, you can move through Week 1 with confidence, but don't skip it.
- If he pushes for heavier loads in Week 1, hold him to the prescribed numbers. Shortening the block to save time usually costs more than it gains.
- Track readiness and resting HR daily through the block, so you have an objective check on how he's really responding.

In short: his enthusiasm is a good sign, and the graded approach will let him return to full loads quickly if he tolerates it. Skipping the reconditioning stage is the one shortcut that's hard to justify.

Readiness for full intensity should be judged by a combination of medical clearance, objective recovery markers, and performance trends across the block, not by how he feels on a single day.

**Gate 1: Medical clearance (non-negotiable)**
- GP review confirming he has fully recovered from the illness.
- Cardiac screening if there are any red flags: chest pain, palpitations, breathlessness out of proportion to effort, dizziness, or exercise intolerance. If there are none, the GP may still consider an ECG reasonable given his age and the illness.
- Written clearance before he returns to heavy or near-maximal work.

**Gate 2: Recovery markers held steady for at least 7 days**
- Resting heart rate within about 5% of his pre-illness baseline, and not rising across sessions.
- Readiness score of 7 or higher most mornings.
- Sleep at 7.5 hours or more most nights.
- No lingering fatigue lasting into the next day after a session.
- Appetite normal and weight trending up at 0.25–0.5 kg per week as planned.

**Gate 3: Performance signals across Weeks 2 and 3**
- Bar speed on the first working set of each lift is consistent with the previous week. Slowing bar speed at the same load is an early warning sign.
- The prescribed RPE is hit at the prescribed load, and the last set of Week 3 (for example, bench at 80 kg for 4 × 4) feels like RPE 7–8, not 9–10.
- Rep quality holds through the set without form breakdown.
- He reports the session as manageable rather than draining.

**Gate 4: Return to 10 km running**
- He has completed the Week 3 running volume and built back to 10 km per week without fatigue carrying into lifting sessions.
- Introduce tempo or interval work only after this.

**Signals to hold back**
- Resting HR rising over several days, or a sustained rise of more than about 10%.
- Readiness repeatedly 4 or lower.
- Performance dropping at the same load across sessions.
- Persistent fatigue, sleep disruption, or new symptoms of any kind.

**Returning to full intensity**
When all four gates are met, the return to heavy work should still be staged. Test with a submaximal estimate first, such as a 3-rep max or a rep-max set at RPE 8. Then move to 85–90% work for 2–3 weeks before attempting true maxes. Rushing to a 1RM test in the first week back is the most common way this goes wrong.

If any stop criterion appears at any point, pull him back a stage and reassess rather than pushing through.

I'd keep the test in Week 3, but not as a true 1RM. Your own gating points to that. Week 3 is still reconditioning, and we haven't confirmed he's medically cleared or that Gate 3 performance holds. A 1RM at the end of Week 3 would also be the "rushed max in the first week back" pattern I flagged earlier.

Instead, use a submaximal test in the back half of Week 3 and estimate his current maxes from it. That gives you real numbers to reset the programme without the risk of a true max.

**Back-half Week 3 test (after the main work, only if Gates 1–2 are met)**

Do this once per lift, at the end of that lift's session:

| Lift | Session | Test | Load | Stop rule |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Bench | Day B | 3 reps after the 4 × 4 @ 80 kg | Start at 85 kg, then 90 kg if the set is easy | Stop at RPE 8 (2 reps in reserve) |
| Squat | Day A | 3 reps after the 4 × 4 @ 112 kg | Start at 117.5 kg, then 122.5 kg if easy | Stop at RPE 8 |
| Deadlift | Day C | 3 reps after the 3 × 3 @ 135 kg | Start at 140 kg, then 145 kg if easy | Stop at RPE 8 |

Use at most two test sets per lift. Take the heaviest set completed with clean form and estimated RPE 8 or below.

**Estimating 1RM**

Use Epley: 1RM ≈ load × (1 + reps / 30). For example, 90 kg × 3 gives about 99 kg. Treat the result as an estimate, and expect it to be within roughly 5% of a true max. Be cautious with it, since fatigue and reconditioning can make it an underestimate.

**Using the results**

- Set Week 4+ training loads at about 80–85% of the estimated 1RM, rather than the pre-illness numbers.
- If the estimates are well below pre-illness levels, that's expected after 3 weeks off plus weight loss. Rebuild from the estimates, not the old maxes.
- If the estimates are close to or above pre-illness levels, still stage the return as described.

**True 1RM test: later, once all four gates are met**

1. Complete 2–3 weeks of work at 85–90% of the estimated 1RM.
2. Confirm bar speed, RPE, and recovery markers are stable.
3. Then schedule a true 1RM test in a fresh session, with a full warm-up, a spotter or safety arms, and at least 3 days since the last heavy session.

Testing a true max at the end of Week 3 would skip the staged return. Using the estimate now gets you the same planning benefit with much less risk.

# 12-Week Reconditioning Block (Weeks 1–3 of Return)

## Before Day 1

- **GP clearance is required before starting.** Post-viral fatigue after a flu-like illness in a 41-year-old warrants a medical check. - **Baseline data:** Record resting HR and a 1–10 readiness score each morning for at least 3 days before starting. Weigh him to establish a starting weight.

- **Daily check:** If resting HR is more than about 10% above baseline, or readiness is 4 or lower, replace that session with light mobility or walking.

**Stop criteria (all weeks):** Fever, chest pain, palpitations, dizziness, unusual breathlessness, or fatigue that worsens across sessions. Stop training and see a doctor.

---

## Week 1: Re-entry (volume ~60%, RPE 5–6)

| Lift | Session | Sets × Reps | Load |

| Back squat | Day A | 3 × 5 | 85 kg |
| Deadlift | Day C | 3 × 3 | 100 kg |

**Warm-ups** (not counted as working sets):

**Day A (Squat focus)**
- Back squat: 3 × 5 @ 85 kg

- Seated dumbbell overhead press: 3 × 8

**Day C (Hinge focus)**

**Load adjustment:** If bar speed is slow on the first working set or he reports lingering fatigue, drop that session's load by 5–10% and keep the rep scheme. If the first working set feels easy, do not add load this week.

**Running (2 sessions, 4 km total):** Tuesday 2 km easy, Saturday 2 km easy. Walk-run (1 × 3 km + 1 × 1 km walk) is an acceptable alternative.

---

## Week 2: Rebuilding (volume ~80%, RPE 6–7)

- Bulgarian split squat: 2 × 8 per leg

- Pallof press: 2 × 10 per side

**Day B (Bench focus)**
- Bench press: 4 × 5 @ 70 kg
- Dumbbell overhead press: 3 × 8
- Cable row: 3 × 10
- Triceps pushdown: 2 × 12
- Face pulls: 2 × 15

**Day C (Hinge focus)**
- Deadlift: 3 × 3 @ 120 kg
- Box squat or paused squat: 3 × 5 @ ~98 kg
- Hip thrust: 3 × 8
- Chin-ups: 3 × 6–8
- Suitcase carry: 3 × 30 m per side

Top sets should feel around RPE 7.

**Running (2 sessions, 6–7 km total):** Tuesday and Saturday, 3–3.5 km easy each. Optional third 2 km easy run on a non-lifting day if he feels well.

---

## Week 3: Return to Baseline (volume ~90%, top sets RPE 7–8)

**Day A (Squat focus)**
- Back squat: 4 × 4 @ 112 kg (last set RPE 8)
- Romanian deadlift: 3 × 8
- Leg press: 3 × 10
- Lat pulldown: 3 × 8
- Ab wheel or dead bug: 2 × 8

**Day B (Bench focus)**
- Bench press: 4 × 4 @ 80 kg (last set RPE 8)
- Incline dumbbell press: 3 × 8
- Chest-supported row: 3 × 8
- Lateral raises: 3 × 12
- Face pulls: 2 × 15

**Day C (Hinge focus)**
- Deadlift: 3 × 3 @ 135 kg (last set RPE 7–8)
- Front squat: 3 × 5
- Walking lunges: 2 × 8 per leg
- Single-arm row: 3 × 8 per side
- Farmer's carry: 3 × 40 m

**Back-half Week 3 submaximal test (only if Gates 1–2 are met).** Do this once per lift, at the end of that lift's session. This is not a 1RM.

| Lift | Session | Test | Load | Stop rule |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Bench | Day B | 3 reps after the 4 × 4 | Start 85 kg, go to 90 kg if easy | Stop at RPE 8 |
| Squat | Day A | 3 reps after the 4 × 4 | Start 117.5 kg, go to 122.5 kg if easy | Stop at RPE 8 |
| Deadlift | Day C | 3 reps after the 3 × 3 | Start 140 kg, go to 145 kg if easy | Stop at RPE 8 |

Use at most two test sets per lift. Take the heaviest set completed with clean form at RPE 8 or below. Estimate 1RM using Epley: 1RM ≈ load × (1 + reps / 30). Expect the estimate to be within about 5% of a true max, and treat it as possibly conservative.

**Running (3 sessions, 8–9 km total):** Tuesday 3 km easy, Thursday 2–3 km easy, Saturday 3 km easy. Four 30-second relaxed strides can close one run.

**Week 3 schedule:**
- Mon: Day A
- Tue: 3 km easy run
- Wed: Day B
- Thu: 2–3 km easy run (or rest)
- Fri: Day C
- Sat: 3 km easy run
- Sun: Rest or walk

---

## Nutrition

Estimates assume ~81 kg bodyweight. Replace with his current weight.

- **Calories:** Maintenance (~2,800–3,100 kcal) plus 200–300 kcal, so about 3,000–3,400 kcal/day. Start at the lower end in Week 1 and move up by Week 3 if weight is not rising.
- **Weight target:** Gain 0.25–0.5 kg per week. If flat for 2 weeks, add ~150 kcal/day. If gaining over 0.5 kg/week, reduce by ~100–150 kcal/day.
- **Protein:** 1.8–2.2 g/kg, roughly 150–175 g/day, in 4 meals of 35–45 g, with an optional pre-bed serving.
- **Carbohydrates:** 4–6 g/kg, roughly 330–490 g/day. Higher on run and lifting days, lower on rest days. Prioritise carbs around sessions.
- **Fats:** 0.8–1.2 g/kg, roughly 65–100 g/day. Do not go below ~0.7 g/kg.
- **Hydration:** 2.5–3 L/day, more on run days and in heat.
- **Micronutrients:** If he still has low appetite or fatigue beyond a few weeks, ask the GP to check ferritin and B12.
- **Monitoring:** Weigh 2–3 times per week under similar conditions and use the weekly average.

## Recovery

- **Sleep:** 7.5–9 hours nightly. This is the most important recovery factor after illness.
- **Morning check:** Resting HR and readiness score (1–10) daily. Log both.
- **Falling performance with weight gain** can indicate under-recovery. Reduce volume before adding food.

---

## Gates to Full Intensity (after Week 3)

Move to the next stage only when all of these are met:

1. **Medical clearance:** Written GP clearance, with an ECG if red flags were present.
2. **Recovery markers stable for 7+ days:** Resting HR within ~5% of baseline and not rising, readiness 7+ most mornings, sleep 7.5+ hours, no next-day fatigue carryover, weight rising 0.25–0.5 kg/week.
3. **Performance:** First working set bar speed consistent week to week, prescribed RPE hit at prescribed loads, clean rep quality, sessions reported as manageable.
4. **Running:** Week 3 volume completed, then built back to 10 km/week over Weeks 4–5 (adding ~1–1.5 km/week) without fatigue carrying into lifting. Tempo or interval work only after this.

**Next stage:** Set working loads at 80–85% of the estimated 1RM. Run 2–3 weeks at 85–90% of the estimate. Then schedule a true 1RM test in a fresh session, with a full warm-up, spotter or safety arms, and at least 3 days since the last heavy session.

If any stop criterion appears at any stage, step back a stage and reassess.

# 12-Week Reconditioning Block (Weeks 1–3 of Return)

## Before Day 1

- **GP clearance is required before starting.** Post-viral fatigue after a flu-like illness in a 41-year-old warrants a medical check. If he has chest pain, palpitations, breathlessness out of proportion to effort, dizziness, or exercise intolerance, he needs an ECG and possibly cardiac workup before any training.
- **Baseline data:** Record resting HR and a 1–10 readiness score each morning for at least 3 days before starting. Weigh him to establish a starting weight.
- **Pre-illness maxes (for reference only):** Bench 100 kg, squat 140 kg, deadlift 170 kg. Week 1 loads are based on these, not used as starting strength.

## Training Structure

- **Lifting:** 3 days per week, at least one rest day between sessions. Rest 2–3 minutes between main lifts.
- **Running:** Runs fall on non-lifting days, at least 6 hours away from any lifting session. Keep all runs at conversational pace (RPE 3–4/10).
- **Daily check:** If resting HR is more than about 10% above baseline, or readiness is 4 or lower, replace that session with light mobility or walking.

**Stop criteria (all weeks):** Fever, chest pain, palpitations, dizziness, unusual breathlessness, or fatigue that worsens across sessions. Stop training and see a doctor.

---

## Week 1: Re-entry (volume ~60%, RPE 5–6)

Stop every set with at least 4 reps in reserve. No grinding reps.

**Working loads:**

| Lift | Session | Sets × Reps | Load |
|---|---|---|---|
| Bench | Day B | 3 × 5 | 60 kg |
| Back squat | Day A | 3 × 5 | 85 kg |
| Deadlift | Day C | 3 × 3 | 100 kg |

**Warm-ups** (not counted as working sets):
- Bench: 1 × 10 empty bar, 1 × 5 at ~30 kg
- Squat: 1 × 8 at ~40 kg, 1 × 5 at ~60 kg, 1 × 3 at ~72 kg
- Deadlift: 1 × 8 at ~50 kg, 1 × 5 at ~70 kg, 1 × 3 at ~85 kg

**Day A (Squat focus)**
- Back squat: 3 × 5 @ 85 kg
- Romanian deadlift: 3 × 8, light-moderate load
- Leg press: 2 × 10
- Lat pulldown: 3 × 10
- Dead bug: 2 × 8 per side

**Day B (Bench focus)**
- Bench press: 3 × 5 @ 60 kg
- Seated dumbbell overhead press: 3 × 8
- Chest-supported row: 3 × 10
- Face pulls: 2 × 15
- Plank: 2 × 30 s

**Day C (Hinge focus)**
- Deadlift: 3 × 3 @ 100 kg
- Goblet squat: 2 × 8
- Walking lunges: 2 × 8 per leg
- Single-arm dumbbell row: 3 × 10 per side
- Farmer's carry: 3 × 30 m

**Load adjustment:** If bar speed is slow on the first working set or he reports lingering fatigue, drop that session's load by 5–10% and keep the rep scheme. If the first working set feels easy, do not add load this week.

**Running (2 sessions, 4 km total):** Tuesday 2 km easy, Saturday 2 km easy. Walk-run (1 × 3 km + 1 × 1 km walk) is an acceptable alternative.

---

## Week 2: Rebuilding (volume ~80%, RPE 6–7)

**Day A (Squat focus)**
- Back squat: 4 × 5 @ 97.5 kg
- Romanian deadlift: 3 × 8, moderate load
- Bulgarian split squat: 2 × 8 per leg
- Pull-ups or assisted pull-ups: 3 × 6–8
- Pallof press: 2 × 10 per side

**Day B (Bench focus)**
- Bench press: 4 × 5 @ 70 kg
- Dumbbell overhead press: 3 × 8
- Cable row: 3 × 10
- Triceps pushdown: 2 × 12
- Face pulls: 2 × 15

**Day C (Hinge focus)**
- Deadlift: 3 × 3 @ 120 kg
- Box squat or paused squat: 3 × 5 @ ~98 kg
- Hip thrust: 3 × 8
- Chin-ups: 3 × 6–8
- Suitcase carry: 3 × 30 m per side

Top sets should feel around RPE 7.

**Running (2 sessions, 6–7 km total):** Tuesday and Saturday, 3–3.5 km easy each. Optional third 2 km easy run on a non-lifting day if he feels well.

---

## Week 3: Return to Baseline (volume ~90%, top sets RPE 7–8)

**Day A (Squat focus)**
- Back squat: 4 × 4 @ 112 kg (last set RPE 8)
- Romanian deadlift: 3 × 8
- Leg press: 3 × 10
- Lat pulldown: 3 × 8
- Ab wheel or dead bug: 2 × 8

**Day B (Bench focus)**
- Bench press: 4 × 4 @ 80 kg (last set RPE 8)
- Incline dumbbell press: 3 × 8
- Chest-supported row: 3 × 8
- Lateral raises: 3 × 12
- Face pulls: 2 × 15

**Day C (Hinge focus)**
- Deadlift: 3 × 3 @ 135 kg (last set RPE 7–8)
- Front squat: 3 × 5
- Walking lunges: 2 × 8 per leg
- Single-arm row: 3 × 8 per side
- Farmer's carry: 3 × 40 m

**Back-half Week 3 submaximal test (only if Gates 1–2 are met).** Do this once per lift, at the end of that lift's session. This is not a 1RM.

| Lift | Session | Test | Load | Stop rule |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Bench | Day B | 3 reps after the 4 × 4 | Start 85 kg, go to 90 kg if easy | Stop at RPE 8 |
| Squat | Day A | 3 reps after the 4 × 4 | Start 117.5 kg, go to 122.5 kg if easy | Stop at RPE 8 |
| Deadlift | Day C | 3 reps after the 3 × 3 | Start 140 kg, go to 145 kg if easy | Stop at RPE 8 |

Use at most two test sets per lift. Take the heaviest set completed with clean form at RPE 8 or below. Estimate 1RM using Epley: 1RM ≈ load × (1 + reps / 30). Expect the estimate to be within about 5% of a true max, and treat it as possibly conservative.

**Running (3 sessions, 8–9 km total):** Tuesday 3 km easy, Thursday 2–3 km easy, Saturday 3 km easy. Four 30-second relaxed strides can close one run.

**Week 3 schedule:**
- Mon: Day A
- Tue: 3 km easy run
- Wed: Day B
- Thu: 2–3 km easy run (or rest)
- Fri: Day C
- Sat: 3 km easy run
- Sun: Rest or walk

---

## Nutrition

Estimates assume ~81 kg bodyweight. Replace with his current weight.

- **Calories:** Maintenance (~2,800–3,100 kcal) plus 200–300 kcal, so about 3,000–3,400 kcal/day. Start at the lower end in Week 1 and move up by Week 3 if weight is not rising.
- **Weight target:** Gain 0.25–0.5 kg per week. If flat for 2 weeks, add ~150 kcal/day. If gaining over 0.5 kg/week, reduce by ~100–150 kcal/day.
- **Protein:** 1.8–2.2 g/kg, roughly 150–175 g/day, in 4 meals of 35–45 g, with an optional pre-bed serving.
- **Carbohydrates:** 4–6 g/kg, roughly 330–490 g/day. Higher on run and lifting days, lower on rest days. Prioritise carbs around sessions.
- **Fats:** 0.8–1.2 g/kg, roughly 65–100 g/day. Do not go below ~0.7 g/kg.
- **Hydration:** 2.5–3 L/day, more on run days and in heat.
- **Micronutrients:** If he still has low appetite or fatigue beyond a few weeks, ask the GP to check ferritin and B12.
- **Monitoring:** Weigh 2–3 times per week under similar conditions and use the weekly average.

## Recovery

- **Sleep:** 7.5–9 hours nightly. This is the most important recovery factor after illness.
- **Morning check:** Resting HR and readiness score (1–10) daily. Log both.
- **Falling performance with weight gain** can indicate under-recovery. Reduce volume before adding food.

---

## Gates to Full Intensity (after Week 3)

Move to the next stage only when all of these are met:

1. **Medical clearance:** Written GP clearance, with an ECG if red flags were present.
2. **Recovery markers stable for 7+ days:** Resting HR within ~5% of baseline and not rising, readiness 7+ most mornings, sleep 7.5+ hours, no next-day fatigue carryover, weight rising 0.25–0.5 kg/week.
3. **Performance:** First working set bar speed consistent week to week, prescribed RPE hit at prescribed loads, clean rep quality, sessions reported as manageable.
4. **Running:** Week 3 volume completed, then built back to 10 km/week over Weeks 4–5 (adding ~1–1.5 km/week) without fatigue carrying into lifting. Tempo or interval work only after this.

**Next stage:** Set working loads at 80–85% of the estimated 1RM. Run 2–3 weeks at 85–90% of the estimate. Then schedule a true 1RM test in a fresh session, with a full warm-up, spotter or safety arms, and at least 3 days since the last heavy session.

If any stop criterion appears at any stage, step back a stage and reassess.
